body:
Small invite-subsystem hygiene items, none urgent:

1. Invite rows for LIVE lists are never purged: expired, used, and revoked
   invites accumulate forever (gc.run only deletes invites when their list is
   hard-deleted). Add a purge of clearly-dead invites (expired/used/revoked
   older than the 90-day retention) to gc.run(). Keep recently-used ones so
   the members screen history stays sensible if ever wanted.
2. invites.mint() validates invited_email as just `"@" in email`, but the
   token payload is colon-delimited (`invite_id:list_id:email:expires_at`,
   split(":", 3)). An email containing ":" mints fine yet produces a token
   that can never decode (expires_at parse fails) — an invite that's dead on
   arrival. Validate with the same EMAIL_RE as registration (or at least
   reject ":"), and add a length cap while at it.
3. The redeem flow's SELECT→UPDATE isn't atomic, but since an invite is bound
   to one email the worst case is the same account redeeming twice —
   INSERT OR IGNORE makes that harmless. No action needed; documenting here
   so the next reader doesn't re-derive it.

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/gc.py,
server/src/shoppinglist_server/invites.py, server/tests/test_invites.py,
server/tests/test_gc.py.
title: Server: invite hygiene — dead invites never purged; colon-in-email mints an undecodable token
